messages.subject: Re: RStan catch?
parts:
On Wednesday, April 10, 2013 2:05:49 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
What I don't understand is that the same model from
the command line does this (this is from an up to date
git pull on the command line in Mac OS X):

=========================================================
~/stan(master)$ make CC=clang++ O=0 ../temp2/crash/mod1

RStan does O=3 by default. I'm pretty sure R wouldn't crash if you reduced the optimization by doing set_cppo("debug") beforehand. What I don't know is why the level of optimization affects how exceptions are handled.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan catch?
parts:
Jiqiang, I don't think you need to change that. The issue is in:
src/stan/math/matrix/check_range.hpp

This is what the definition of check_range looks like:
    inline
    void check_range(size_t max,
                     size_t i,
                     const char* msg,
                     size_t idx) {
#ifndef NDEBUG
      if (i < 1 || i > max)
        raise_range_error(max,i,msg,idx);
#endif
    }


I'm going to remove the #ifndef and we won't have this problem.



Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan catch?
parts:
On Wednesday, April 10, 2013 1:39:41 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
Jiqiang, I don't think you need to change that. The issue is in:
src/stan/math/matrix/check_range.hpp

This is what the definition of check_range looks like:
    inline
    void check_range(size_t max,
                     size_t i,
                     const char* msg,
                     size_t idx) {
#ifndef NDEBUG
      if (i < 1 || i > max)
        raise_range_error(max,i,msg,idx);
#endif
    }


I'm going to remove the #ifndef and we won't have this problem.

But then we have the problem that we can't turn the checks off. There was some discussion about adding STAN_DEBUG to have finer grained control of things like this, but I don't know what happened with that. My view is that if someone sets set_cppo("fast") without first verifying that their model is correct, then they deserve to crash. Maybe RStan could set -DDEBUG unless the user calls set_cppo("fast") instead of what we do now which is only set -DDEBUG if the user calls set_cppo("debug").

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan catch?
parts: On Wed, Apr 10, 2013 at 2:01 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

On Wednesday, April 10, 2013 1:39:41 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
Jiqiang, I don't think you need to change that. The issue is in:
src/stan/math/matrix/check_range.hpp

This is what the definition of check_range looks like:
    inline
    void check_range(size_t max,
                     size_t i,
                     const char* msg,
                     size_t idx) {
#ifndef NDEBUG
      if (i < 1 || i > max)
        raise_range_error(max,i,msg,idx);
#endif
    }


I'm going to remove the #ifndef and we won't have this problem.

But then we have the problem that we can't turn the checks off. There was some discussion about adding STAN_DEBUG to have finer grained control of things like this, but I don't know what happened with that. My view is that if someone sets set_cppo("fast") without first verifying that their model is correct, then they deserve to crash. Maybe RStan could set -DDEBUG unless the user calls set_cppo("fast") instead of what we do now which is only set -DDEBUG if the user calls set_cppo("debug").

First, we can handle checks using policies. That refactoring is high on my list.

Regarding use case, I don't think the users understand the contract that you've described with using set_cppo("fast"). Unless it's really clear to the user that set_cppo("fast") can crash R and setting it is very deliberate, I think the behavior should be to not crash rstan. Is that range check really killing speed? Naively, I would think that other parts of Stan would dominate time.

That is the only check function that has a #ifndef. I think it's better to be consistent about our error checking. I believe the right thing to do is to use the global policy to dictate how / when to handle errors.

for some classes of models we're starting to see checks like this one
in the profiles.

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan catch?
parts:
-DNDEBUG is set by R (not RStan) by default.  So if the user does not use set_cppo() at all, R will use O2 for optimization level and set -DNDEBUG.  

I need to see if I can overwrite that flag set by R when stan() gets called.  If yes, adding an option such as DEBUG=TRUE for stan() would be good.  But this option would be overwritten by what is configured by set_cppo().

--
Jiqiang
On Thu, Apr 11, 2013 at 12:00 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

I'm happy for there to be a way for the checks to be turned
off.  But it shouldn't be the default install option for
RStan.

So a set_cppo("fast") option would be OK with me, as long
as it prints out some warnings to the user that doing so may
crash the R process if their model has bugs.

- Bob
On 4/10/13 2:01 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:

On Wednesday, April 10, 2013 1:39:41 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:

    Jiqiang, I don't think you need to change that. The issue is in:
    src/stan/math/matrix/check_range.hpp

    This is what the definition of check_range looks like:
         inline
         void check_range(size_t max,
                          size_t i,
                          const char* msg,
                          size_t idx) {
    #ifndef NDEBUG
           if (i < 1 || i > max)
             raise_range_error(max,i,msg,idx);
    #endif
         }


    I'm going to remove the #ifndef and we won't have this problem.


But then we have the problem that we can't turn the checks off. There was some discussion about adding STAN_DEBUG to
have finer grained control of things like this, but I don't know what happened with that. My view is that if someone
sets set_cppo("fast") without first verifying that their model is correct, then they deserve to crash. Maybe RStan could
set -DDEBUG unless the user calls set_cppo("fast") instead of what we do now which is only set -DDEBUG if the user calls
set_cppo("debug").

Ben

I think this is okay for v1.3, but without -NDEBUG, the .cpp code will check the indices of a matrix access twice, once with Stan functions and once with Eigen functions. But that is more of a Stan problem than a RStan problem.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan catch?
parts:
There's an Eigen-specific flag we should be using
to turn off their error bounds. -DNDEBUG turns off
their bounds checking, too, but we can just turn off
their bounds checks. (We don't need to use Eigen's
checks because we check everything before sending it
to Eigen.)

We'll get that into the next release.

- Bob
